Author: Ajit Kumar

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:159940
Court No. - 4
Case :- Writ - A No. - 56050 of 2014
Petitioner :- Satish Chandra And 12 Ors
Respondent :- Union Of India And 2 Ors

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- A.S.G.I.,Madhur Prakash,P.C. Joshi,S.C.
Hon'ble Ajit Kumar,J.
1.

Heard Sri Hriday Narayan Pandey, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Madhur Prakash,
learned counsel for the respondent Nos. 2 & 3.
2.

By means of this petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution, petitioners seek quashing of the order dated 12th September, 2014 passed by the General Manager GAIL, namely respondent No.- 2, whereby a communication addressed to the officer of the department with the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has been made about the status of the petitioners qua employment at the GAIL and the decision in that regard earlier taken by the concerned respondent on 25th April,
2014 rejecting representation of the petitioner.

entities.text: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
This order rejecting the representation has also been Satish Chandra And 12 Ors vs Union Of India And 2 Ors on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161776636/
1 challenged by way of amendment application.
3. The submission advanced by learned counsel for the petitioner is that the respondents had entered an agreement with the petitioners - tenure holders, whose lands were acquired by way of compulsory acquisition under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and understanding was reached on 29th June, 1998 while signing the agreement by the officers of the Gas Authority of India Ltd. and District Magistrate that appointments will be offered to the tenure holders in lieu of the acquisition of their land. He submits that authorities having not acted upon the agreement and offered only a contract appointment to the petitioners for some period of time, GAIL has breached the contract and now wholly and illegally a stand was taken that as and when the vacancy would arise at the GAIL the appointment will be offered as per the relevant rules inviting applications through open market as well taking recourse to publication in newspaper.

entities.text: Satish Chandra And 12 Ors vs Union Of India And 2 Ors on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He submits that the respondents,
therefore, deserved to be commanded to abide by the agreement entered between the tenure holders and the authorities of the GAIL as well as District Magistrate concerned.
4. One of the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the petitioners is also that District Magistrate being an authority of the State and Gas Authority of India Ltd. being state company of the Central Government both should honour the agreement reached with the petitioners and breach of the same can be questioned even before this Court under Article 226 of the Constitution.
5.

entities.text: State and Gas Authority of India Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Per contra, it is submitted by learned counsel for the respondents, namely GAIL authorities that controversy as to claim for employment in lieu of compulsory acquisition of land is no more res integra.

He submits that even though there was a Government order issued by the State Government to provide for compassionate appointment in the matter of compulsory acquisition of land but the law was already held to by this Court as well as by Supreme Court as ultra vires Article 14 of the Constitution for in matters of public employment no back door entry like this kind could be permitted, moreso, where in lieu of acquisition of land, the compensation has been paid to the tenure holders.

Even in a matter of GAIL he has cited a judgment of Division Bench of this Court in the case of Gas Authority of India through its Deputy General Manager, Dibiyapur, Etawah v. State of U.P. and others, (2004) 1 UPLBEC 73, wherein a similar argument raised was that in the light of the State Government's decision to offer employment in lieu of the compulsory acquisition of land,
the authority cannot just get rid of its liability in the matter.

The Court rejected the argument on the ground that there being no provision under the relevant service rules governing service conditions in employment and recruitment procedure, by an execute fiat, no direction could be issued for a back door entry.

The Court in that case had disagreed with the view taken by the learned Single Judge in the case of Umesh Chandra Srivastava v. District Magistrate, Gorakhpur in Civil Misc. Writ Petition No.- 28795 of 1992 decided on 14th February, 1994.

entities.text: Umesh Chandra Srivastava v. District Magistrate, Gorakhpur
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Civil Misc. Writ Petition No.- 28795 of 1992
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
Vide paragraphs 15, 16, 17 and 18 of the judgment of Gas Authority of India (supra) the Court has held thus:
"15.
With profound respect to the learned Single Judge we are not in agreement with the view he has taken.
The learned Single Judge has adopted an approach which is mere emotional rather than legal.

A writ is issued for violation of law or enforcement of some legal duty, and not on such vague and general considerations that since the Government is a welfare State it has to provide a job to a person whose land is Satish Chandra And 12 Ors vs Union Of India And 2 Ors on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161776636/
2 acquired.

entities.text: Satish Chandra And 12 Ors vs Union Of India And 2 Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As already stated above, the person whose land is acquired is not only given full market value with interest from the date of the Notification under Section 4, but is also given 30% solatium on top of that.

If the Legislature intended that apart from the above, the affected person should also be provided a job to a member of his family then such a provision would have been made in the Land Acquisition Act.

16. Learned counsel for the respondents has relied on the Supreme Court decision in Calcutta Port Trust v. Deba Prosad Bag, AIR 1994 SC 2137 and Banwasi Seva Ashram v. State of U.P., AIR 1992 SC 920.
17.

entities.text: Calcutta Port Trust v. Deba Prosad Bag, AIR 1994 SC 2137
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Banwasi Seva Ashram v. State of U.P., AIR 1992 SC 920
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In our opinion, the aforesaid decisions do not lay down any principle of law that on acquisition of land under the Land Acquisition Act apart from giving compensation under the Act a job has also to be provided.
It is well-settled that a mere direction in a judgment without laying down any principle of law is not a precedent vide AIR 2002 SC 3088 : 2003 (1) ESC 424, etc.
Hence, the aforesaid decisions are not a precedent.

18. Moreover, as rightly stated by the appellant, the nature of a job in the Gas Authority of India Ltd. is a highly technical one and if unqualified people are appointed there can be danger to the public.

Hence, also the stand of the appellant is correct."
6.
Upon a pointed query being learned counsel for the petitioner could not dispute the legal position as discussed above.
However, he seeks liberty to apply for a common law remedy for enforcement of the agreement.
7. In the considered view of the Court, the common law remedy is always available subject to the limitation prescribed under the law and hence no special order for liberty is required.
8. It is always open for the petitioners to pursue the remedy if available other than approaching this Court under Article 226 of the Constitution again.
9. Subject to aforesaid liberty, the petition is consigned to records.
